description: Dull band-like pressure around the head with neck tightness, linked to stress or poor sleep, without vomiting or aura.

caution: Seek care for sudden severe headache, fever with stiff neck, weakness or vision changes.

description: Hives, itching, swollen lips or a tingling mouth, sometimes with vomiting or stomach cramps, soon after eating a food the person may be allergic to, without breathing difficulty.

recommendation: Stop eating the suspected food and keep the packaging or a note of what was eaten. See a doctor the same day to confirm the trigger and learn how to avoid it. Stay with the person and watch them closely for the next few hours.

caution: If the person has trouble breathing, swelling of the throat or tongue, or fainting, call emergency services. If the medicine was prescribed for a serious illness, ask the prescriber what to take instead rather than going without.

condition: Severe Drug Reaction with Skin Blistering (Stevens-Johnson type)

source: Allergy & Immunology Reference Set (draft, pending clinician review)
recommendation: This is a medical emergency. Go to a hospital immediately and stop the suspected medicine; take the medicine box or strips with you.

description: Pain, redness, swelling and itching at the site of a bee, wasp, ant or other insect sting or bite, without symptoms elsewhere in the body.

recommendation: Wash the area with plain water and gentle soap and avoid the suspected trigger. Keep the skin moisturised. See a health worker if it does not improve in a week or keeps coming back.

recommendation: Moisturise regularly, use mild soap, keep nails short and avoid known triggers such as harsh soaps and wool. A health worker can advise on treatment for flares.

review_status: DRAFT - requires licensed clinician review before any real-world use

description: Both eyes itchy, red, watery and slightly swollen, often with sneezing, triggered by dust or pollen, without thick sticky discharge.

recommendation: Avoid rubbing the eyes, rinse with clean cool water, use a cold cloth and reduce exposure to dust or pollen. A pharmacist or health worker can advise on allergy eye drops.

condition: Angioedema (Swelling of Lips, Face or Tongue)

description: Itchy scalp with visible tiny lice or white egg cases (nits) stuck to the hair near the scalp, common in children.

recommendation: Treat with a lice product recommended by a pharmacist or health worker and comb the hair with a fine-toothed comb. Wash bedding and combs in hot water and check close contacts.

description: Bleeding from one or both nostrils, often from dry air, nose picking, a minor knock or a cold.

condition: Suspected Rabies (Symptoms After an Animal Bite)
description: Weeks or months after an animal bite or scratch: fever, tingling at the bite site, fear of water or drinking, throat spasms, drooling, agitation or confusion.
source: Infectious & Tropical Disease Reference Set (draft, pending clinician review)
recommendation: Go to a hospital immediately. Rabies is almost always fatal once symptoms start, so urgent medical care and isolation are essential. Caregivers should avoid contact with saliva and seek vaccination advice.
caution: Do not rely on home or traditional remedies. Wash any saliva contact with soap and water. Prevention (vaccination after any bite) is the only protection.
